problem: Prior instruction-navigation methods each handle only one instruction type: ObjectNav explores to find an object, VLN follows step-by-step routes, and DDN reasons about human demands. Training a single model for all of them is blocked by scarce data, so no system could run different instruction types zero-shot in continuous, unmapped environments.
motivation: Robots that accept arbitrary language instructions would be far more useful, but each task needs a different strategy: efficient exploration, route following, or commonsense reasoning. The authors observe that any navigation instruction can be written as an 'Action → Landmark' chain. This mirrors LLM chain-of-thought, so an LLM can unify planning, and spatial value maps can ground that plan into trajectories without any navigation training.
key_idea: At every decision step, re-plan the next (action, landmark) with an LLM ('Dynamic Chain-of-Navigation'). Ground it by summing four value maps (action, semantic, trajectory, GPT-4V 'intuition') over the navigable point cloud, then pick the argmax point as the next waypoint.
insight: Re-planning the landmark chain against the objects actually observed does three things: it aligns instruction words to segmentation labels (e.g. 'arched wooden doors' → 'Doorway'), it drives exploration when the target is unseen, and it converts abstract demands ('I am thirsty' → bottle of water) into concrete targets. Removing DCoN drops SR from 56→44 (ObjNav), 30→23 (R2R-CE) and 33→22 (DDN) on 100-episode subsets. The value maps matter differently per task: the Semantic map dominates ObjectNav (56→44 without it), while the GPT-4V Intuition map matters most for R2R-CE (SR 30→17) and DDN (33→20). Without the Intuition map on R2R-CE, OSR rises to 47 but SR falls to 17, i.e. the agent passes the goal and fails to stop, so the MLM mainly contributes precise direction choice and stopping. Swapping in open-source Llama3-70B + LLaVA-1.6-34B roughly holds on ObjectNav (SR 50 vs 56) but collapses on R2R-CE (12 vs 30). Replacing the multimodal model hurts VLN most (OSR 42→26), and replacing the LLM hurts DDN most (33→21).
method: Dynamic Chain-of-Navigation (DCoN): GPT-4 (gpt-4-0613) is re-queried at every decision step. The prompt has four parts: Robot Definition, Navigation Strategy (candidate actions such as Explore/Approach/Move Forward, landmark requirements favouring observed objects, per-task strategy text), Prediction Format, and Episode Information. The output is {'Reason','Action','Landmark','Flag'} giving the next action A_i and landmarks L_i; Flag=True means stop.

Semantic Value Map: GLEE 2D segmentation masks are lifted to a 3D semantic point cloud using depth and pose. Each navigable point gets value 1 − normalized min-distance to the points of landmark L_i, so areas near the landmark score high.

Action Value Map: set by action type. Move forward / turn around / right / left put value 1 on the front / back / right / left quarter-sector of the panoramic FOV. Explore puts value 1 on frontier boundaries. Enter/Exit are rewritten as Approach + 'Doorway' landmark. Approach leaves this map unchanged and relies on the Semantic map.
Trajectory Value Map: normalized min-distance from each navigable point to the history trajectory, so unvisited areas score higher and repetition is discouraged.

Intuition Value Map: 6 of 12 directional RGB views (every other view), each annotated with a direction ID, are concatenated into a panorama. GPT-4V receives the full instruction plus A_i and L_i, reasons with CoT, and picks a direction. That direction's FOV gets value 1 on navigable points; if none are navigable, failure feedback triggers re-prediction.

Decision & control: m = m_i + m_a + m_t + m_s, with obstacles zeroed. The argmax point becomes the waypoint and A* plans the path over m. In simulation a rotate-then-forward controller (from ETPNav) tracks the path with discrete actions; the real robot uses velocity control via Nav2 with SLAM Toolbox localization. Navigation stops when the DCoN Flag is True or GPT-4V outputs Stop.

setting.backbone: GPT-4 (gpt-4-0613) for DCoN planning + GPT-4V (gpt-4-vision-preview) for the Intuition map, both frozen with OpenAI default parameters. GLEE supplies semantic segmentation. Ablation variants use Llama3 70B and/or LLaVA-1.6 (LLaVA-NeXT) 34B.
setting.training_data: none (training-free; no navigation training, no pre-built maps)
setting.observation: egocentric RGB-D + camera pose; multi-direction RGB views (12 directions, 6 given to GPT-4V) at each decision step
setting.action_space: predicted waypoints (argmax of summed value map) tracked by an A* path. Simulation uses discrete rotate-then-forward actions; the real robot uses continuous velocity via Nav2.
setting.simulator: Habitat (HM3D ObjectNav, R2R-CE); AI2-THOR with ProcTHOR scenes (DDN)
setting.privileged: ground-truth camera pose in simulation (SLAM Toolbox localization on the real robot); no GT maps or semantics

numbers_note: The HM3D ObjectNav split and episode count are not stated; the paper only says it follows the Habitat ObjectNav challenge setting, so val is assumed. The DDN split is described only as 'unseen scenes and unseen instructions' and is mapped here to test-unseen. The N-views ablation (N=4/6/12) appears only in a figure without numbers. Mixed-backbone variants (Llama3 70B + GPT4V; GPT4 + LLaVA1.6 34B) are in Table 5 but omitted here. The abstract's '10.48%' and '86.34%' gains are relative SR improvements (58.0 vs 52.5; 30.0 vs 16.1). Real-robot experiments are qualitative only. Table 1 labels VLFM as 'VLMF' with the L3MVN citation.
results: The same training-free system runs three task types. On HM3D ObjectNav it reaches SR 58.0 / SPL 20.9 / NE 2.58, beating the best zero-shot baseline VLFM (SR 52.5) on success but not on SPL (VLFM 30.4), and approaching trained OVRL (SR 62.0). On R2R-CE val-unseen it is the first zero-shot result: SR 31, SPL 24, NE 6.89. This beats several trained models without MP3D waypoint predictors (CWP-CMA 27, Ego2Map-NaViT 30) but trails CMA (32) and NaVid (37). On DDN it gets SR 30.0 / SPL 14.2 versus the trained DDN baseline at 16.1 / 8.4.
limitations: Best performance depends on closed-source GPT-4/GPT-4V. Open-source Llama3-70B + LLaVA-1.6-34B drops R2R-CE SR from 30 to 12 on the ablation subset.
Path efficiency is low: ObjectNav SPL is 20.9 versus VLFM's 30.4. Each step needs multi-direction views and multiple LLM/MLM calls, and the semantic value map suffers under occlusion.
The R2R-CE comparison deliberately excludes methods using MP3D-trained waypoint predictors (e.g. ETPNav, BEVBert), which score much higher. Real-robot results are qualitative only.
